root_cause: No pprof endpoint is exposed; the audit's §8.2 prerequisite and the checklist's G item both flag this.
impact: Cannot run go tool pprof http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile to capture CPU/heap/block profiles during a Claude Code session or any reproduction. The audit therefore cannot validate any wakeup/memory hypothesis, and end-users cannot diagnose regressions without rebuilding from source.
fix_sketch: In startup() start `go func() { _ = http.ListenAndServe("localhost:6060", nil) }()` with `import _ "net/http/pprof"`. Gate on dev builds (e.g. const dev = Version == "dev") so production builds don't open a listener.
verification: go tool pprof http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 with the audit's recording template; verify the symbol list contains wails_bridge.* and session.OutputLogger.* paths.

root_cause: App startup installs no macOS lifecycle hooks (WillResignActive / DidResignActive / window blur), so every ticker, retry-backoff, K8s watch resync, AI stream keepalive and update-check interval keeps firing while the app is backgrounded.
impact: Amplifies the 900+/s idle wakeup measurement when the user backgrounds the app: every Wails callback loop, AI retry, sync poll, k8s watch reconnect and output-log fsync continues unabated. macOS App Nap cannot kick in because nothing signals 'I'm idle', so the OS treats the app as busy and refuses to throttle. CPU drain on laptops and unnecessary battery use.
fix_sketch: Wire `runtime.EventsOn(ctx, "wails:window:focus")` / `runtime.EventsOn(ctx, "wails:window:blur")` (and the macOS-specific lifecycle emitter if available) into a `app.active` flag; have each subsystem pause its tickers when `!active`. In main.go set `Mac.HideOption` so the menu bar also stops animations on hide.
verification: Instruments / `log show --predicate 'process == "uniTerm"'` while minimising for 30s: confirm timer wakeup count drops. Locally, add a counter incremented in each ticker and log on resume; expect zero ticks during background.

root_cause: SyncNow / SyncTestConnection / SyncVerifyPassword / SyncConfigureRepo / SyncChangePassword / SyncDeleteRepo block the Wails handler thread on synchronous git + network + crypto work.
impact: Every SaveConnections / SaveSettings triggers a.triggerAutoSync() (line 350, 488, 786). A user editing a connection field while online stalls the entire UI for the duration of git push+pull + AES-GCM decryption. With auto-sync enabled this happens on EVERY store mutation.
fix_sketch: Return immediately with a request-id and run the sync in a goroutine; emit 'sync:started' / 'sync:completed' / 'sync:failed' events. Frontend already listens on 'sync:completed' so no breaking change. Add coalescing: only one sync in flight at a time, drop new triggers while running.
verification: Add log.Writef timestamp markers; measure Wails handler round-trip latency in DevTools Network before/after — SyncNow should return <5ms instead of the sync duration.

root_cause: SaveConnections emits the FULL ConnectionStoreData (every connection + group + recent) over the bridge on every save; the same full payload is then re-loaded by reloadStoresAfterSync on the next sync tick.
impact: Connection lists grow unboundedly; emit payloads measured in 100s of KB for moderate users, MB-scale for power users. WebKit has to structured-clone the entire blob into JS land on every keystroke that triggers SaveConnections. Compounds with the 400 MB WebKit memory baseline — each emit can be retained until GC.
fix_sketch: Emit only the diff or change kind: `{ kind: 'upsert' | 'remove', id, connection? }`. On sync reload, keep the full blob (it really did change) but compress with `sync/atomic` or only emit when the frontend's view isn't current. Add `omitempty` on zero-value struct fields so unused protocol blobs don't ship.
verification: Chrome DevTools → Performance recording during a SaveConnections burst; look for 'structured clone' marker duration and heap delta. Compare payload size in DevTools Network (Wails frame size) before/after.

root_cause: SetOnDataCallback allocates a fresh map[string]interface{} per chunk and copies []byte to string (escapes to heap) for every terminal output byte chunk that crosses the bridge.
impact: Per active terminal this is the single hottest allocation site. Claude Code's spinner phase emits many small chunks per second; each chunk triggers: 1 map alloc, 1 string copy (escaped heap), 2 interface boxings, and a Wails JSON marshal + WebKit structured-clone. For 4 concurrent terminals at 50 chunks/s this is millions of allocs/s. Directly contributes to the 400 MB resident set.
fix_sketch: Replace EventsEmit with a session-scoped Go channel + dedicated goroutine that uses json.NewEncoder on a sync.Pool'd buffer. Carry the bytes as base64 in a fixed-size struct (no interface map). Better: have the frontend subscribe to a binary protocol over a per-session WebSocket and decode there. Minimum change: drop the map and pass `(sID, []byte)` to a wrapper that constructs the map once per emit and reuses a string-builder.
verification: go test -bench=BenchmarkSessionEmit -benchmem ./backend/session/... — record allocs/op before and after. pprof heap inuse_objects on `runtime.EventsEmit` should drop to <1% of total.

root_cause: moveResizeCh goroutine launched in startup() never receives a shutdown signal — it lives for the process lifetime, blocking on a channel that is never closed.
impact: A leaked long-lived goroutine per app instance (always 1). Itself minor, but it's a sign the lifecycle model is ad-hoc: every other goroutine spawned in startup() is the same — `go a.autoStartTunnels()`, `go func() { syncSvc.Sync() }()`. When the user quits the app, none of these observe the ctx cancellation, so in-flight sync / tunnel bring-up can race with shutdown()'s os.RemoveAll(webviewDataPath) and produce 'sync failed' log lines.
fix_sketch: Add `defer close(a.moveResizeCh)` (or signal via select { <-ctx.Done(): close(ch) }) in the goroutine body, and `close(a.moveResizeCh)` in shutdown(). For one-shot startup goroutines, branch on ctx.Done() before kicking off heavy work.
verification: kill -QUIT the process during a slow sync; pprof goroutine count should drop to baseline within 1s.

root_cause: triggerAutoSync spawns a fresh `go func()` on every store mutation with no coalescing or in-flight tracking, so a burst of saves (e.g. pasting 50 commands into QuickCommands) launches 50 concurrent syncs.
impact: N concurrent git pulls against the same repo corrupt the worktree lock (`.git/index.lock` collisions), each leaves a sync:completed event the frontend has to handle, and the underlying sync.Sync() does not guard against concurrent invocation. Wakes up the goroutine scheduler ~10x more than needed during edits.
fix_sketch: Add a single `syncInFlight sync.atomic.Bool` flag — if set, return immediately. When the sync completes, clear the flag and re-check whether another trigger came in during the run; if so, kick one more. Cap concurrent syncs at 1.
verification: Burst-call SaveConnections 50x from a test; observe in log that syncService.Sync runs at most 2x (1 initial + 1 coalesced), not 50. Concurrent burst-test should pass.

root_cause: chatCompletion* methods construct `&http.Client{Timeout: 0}` per call; no keep-alive, no connection pool — every LLM request opens a fresh TCP+TLS handshake.
impact: Anthropic/OpenAI endpoints require TLS; reconnecting every turn adds ~100-300ms of TLS handshake + TCP slow-start on top of the actual model latency. Across a multi-turn Claude Code session this is several seconds of pure overhead. Wakes the scheduler 2-3 extra times per request (TCP/TLS goroutines).
fix_sketch: Hoist a single `*http.Client` with `Transport: &http.Transport{TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{...}, MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 4, IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second}` to a sync.Once-built App-scoped field. Reset idle conns on shutdown. Streamed bodies do not need the client to be closed mid-flight.
verification: Time three consecutive ChatCompletion calls with curl-equivalent payload. First call 100% handshake, subsequent should reuse (observe via `tcpdump -i lo0 -nn`).

root_cause: Unbounded `io.ReadAll(res.Body)` on the error path of LLM proxies — a malicious or misconfigured upstream can return a multi-GB error body and the Go side will buffer it all on the Wails handler goroutine.
impact: OOM-or-allocator-pressure risk on the Wails handler goroutine when the LLM provider returns a huge error blob (CDN HTML page, captive-portal redirect, accidental binary response). Hits on every failed chat turn.
fix_sketch: Wrap with `io.LimitReader(res.Body, 64<<10)`; on overflow append `... [truncated N bytes]`. Apply to all three chatCompletion helpers and FetchModels.
verification: Stub server returning 10 MB body; observe allocation count via go test -bench and runtime.MemStats.

root_cause: Every ai:done emit and the final return value both json.Marshal the full message map from scratch, with the same contentBlocks slice; double work per turn.
impact: Per chat turn the full message (often 10-100KB for a Claude Code reply) is marshalled twice. With rapid tool-use turns the JSON-encode cost is non-trivial, and the same payload is structured-cloned twice in WebKit (once from emit, once from the return value).
fix_sketch: Marshal once into a pooled buffer; reuse the resulting JSON for both the emit and the return. Better: skip the EventsEmit payload entirely for the final message and let the frontend pick up the return value through the promise resolution (which it already does).

root_cause: SaveConnections / SaveSettings / SaveTunnels / SaveQuickCommands / SaveAIConfig all run a.fs-fsync on the Wails handler thread (atomic-rename write inside store.Save) before the emit; combined with F-203/207 this stalls the UI on every save.
impact: Editor save → ~5-50 ms blocking (depends on fsync + connection-list size); combined with triggerAutoSync that can extend to seconds during auto-sync. Add up to per-keystroke for settings sliders bound to SaveSettings.
fix_sketch: Run a.connectionStore.Save in a goroutine; return immediately with a request-id; emit 'store:saved' (or just 'store:connections:changed' if Save was best-effort with eventual consistency). For settings where the user expects persistence confirmation, keep Save sync but make SaveConnections async.
verification: DevTools Performance recording while typing in a settings field; expect handler round-trip <2 ms instead of disk-fsync time.

root_cause: panelLogTitle and EnableSessionOutputLog both scan the entire sessionToPanel map (keyed by sessionID) to find the one bound to a panelID — O(n) per enable on every Enable call.
impact: Marginal: called on Enable/Disable only, not hot. Becomes O(n) when many sessions are bound to different panels (each reopen of a session rebinds). P2.
fix_sketch: Maintain a parallel `panelToSession map[string]string` updated under the same mutex. Or invert to a session-keyed slice and update on bind/unbind.
verification: Unit bench on n=10/100/1000 active sessions.

root_cause: ListSessions returns every SessionInfo in the manager on each call; if the frontend polls this (it does — see panelStore and tabStore cross-checks) it produces a steady stream of allocations even when nothing has changed.
impact: Each call allocates a fresh slice; on long-running sessions the garbage keeps accumulating. P2 because call frequency is moderate and the slice is small.
fix_sketch: Either deprecate ListSessions and emit session:status events only on change, or memoize the last result and short-circuit when no underlying status changed.
verification: Inspect store call sites; if a computed/listener wraps ListSessions in a watch, refactor to subscribe to session:status.
